Article Title: ICMR picks 7 centres to develop priority medical devices, diagnostics
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Seven research centres across leading Indian institutions have been selected by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to develop priority medical devices and diagnostic technologies, with projects spanning portable screening for primary healthcare, biomaterials and technologies for eye and vascular diseases.The selected institutions are the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) at Kharagpur, Delhi, Bombay, Kanpur and Madras, the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Coimbatore.Among the selected projects, IIT Bombay's centre, led by Dr Abhijit Majumder, will focus on portable screening, monitoring and point-of-care medical technologies for primary healthcare. Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham's centre, led by Prof Gopal S Pillai, will work on developing, validating and translating healthcare technologies for ophthalmic and vascular diseases, while IISc Bengaluru will focus on biomaterials and translational medical devices.IIT Kharagpur's PRAGATICAR, led by Prof Suman Chakraborty, will focus on frugal diagnostics, regenerative and personalised healthcare, artificial intelligence, digital health and advanced therapeutics. IIT Delhi's CAR-PATH, led by Prof Vivekanandan Perumal, will work on priority applied technologies for healthcare.At IIT Kanpur, Prof Amitabha Bandyopadhyay will lead a multidisciplinary proposal to develop 10 priority healthcare products.IIT Madras will host TARaNGaM, a translational hub for next-generation medical technology, devices and diagnostics, led by Prof Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam.The initiative aims to accelerate the development of affordable, accessible and indigenous healthcare technologies addressing unmet clinical needs. To identify these needs, ICMR undertook an exercise involving clinicians from different healthcare settings, including tier-1, tier-2 and tier-3 cities, and drew up a curated list of around 100 priority medical device and diagnostic technologies.Under the original call for proposals, applicants were required to propose the development of at least eight to 10 technologies from this list, covering a mix of low-risk and high-risk products. The scheme provides for funding of up to Rs 15 crore per centre over five years, with an emphasis on regulatory-compliant product development and eventual commercialisation.The call prioritised institutions with a track record in research, prototyping, technology transfer and commercialisation. It also required centres to leverage existing infrastructure, build a trained medical technology research workforce and continue functioning beyond the funding period, with host institutions expected to sustain them as permanent activities.The key challenge will be translating research into validated products that can address clinical needs and reach patients. The results list does not specify the individual devices to be developed by most of the selected centres, their development timelines or when the technologies could become available for clinical use.
Article Summary: Seven research centres selected by Indian Council of Medical Research to develop priority medical devices and diagnostic technologies. The selected institutions are the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) at Kharagpur, Delhi, Bombay, Kanpur and Madras. The initiative aims to accelerate the development of affordable, accessible and indigenous healthcare technologies addressing unmet clinical needs.

Article Title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
Article Text:
Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party.

1. Yashwant Sinha

2. Ajit Jogi

3. Mani Shankar Aiyar

4. Arvind Kejriwal

5. KJ Alphons

6. Satyapal Singh

7. OP Choudhary

8. Aparajita Sarangi

9. AK Sharma

10. Asim Arun

Bonus: K Annamalai

NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career to pursue politics independently.In a video message on X, Mittal said the party will focus on making people central to policymaking and ensuring that the government remains accountable to them throughout its five-year term, rather than only on election day."Politics rules over you. In Jan Neeti, you will be the ones who rule," she said, announcing the party's name and its decision to contest the state polls due early next year.Her decision to launch a party of her own places her among a group of civil servants who left government service before their scheduled retirement to enter politics.Here are 10 former civil servants who made the transition from bureaucracy to politics before completing their service.Yashwant Sinha resigned from the Indian Administrative Service in 1984 to enter active politics. He joined the Janata Party and subsequently became associated with the Janata Dal before joining the BJP.Sinha first served as Union finance minister in the Chandra Shekhar government in 1990-91.Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he returned to the finance ministry in 1998 and held the portfolio until 2002, when he became external affairs minister.His political career also included membership of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Sinha later distanced himself from the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress in 2021, before contesting the 2022 presidential election as the opposition's joint candidate.Ajit Jogi left the IAS in 1986 to enter politics and joined the Congress. He had served as a district collector before moving into political life and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha.Jogi's biggest political breakthrough came in 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh. He became the newly created state's first chief minister, holding office until 2003.After years in the Congress, Jogi broke away from the party in 2016 and founded the Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, seeking to establish an independent regional political platform.His career stands out as an example of a former administrator moving from district-level governance to the leadership of a newly formed state and later attempting to build a party of his own.Mani Shankar Aiyar resigned from the Indian Foreign Service in 1989 to enter politics. He had served as a diplomat for more than two decades and spent part of his career on deputation to the Prime Minister's Office under Rajiv Gandhi.Aiyar joined the Congress and won the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha seat in Tamil Nadu in 1991. He went on to become a prominent party leader and served as Union minister for petroleum and natural gas during the UPA government.He also held the panchayati raj portfolio and was involved in efforts to strengthen local self-government institutions.Arvind Kejriwal resigned from the Indian Revenue Service in 2006 after working in the income tax department. He had become involved in the Right to Information movement and founded the non-governmental organisation Parivartan to address citizens' grievances.His political journey gathered momentum during the Ana Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which campaigned for a stronger anti-corruption law. In 2012, Kejriwal founded the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), choosing to build a political organisation rather than join an established party.AAP made its electoral debut in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, when Kejriwal defeated then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He became Delhi chief minister in December 2013 and returned to the post after the party's victories in 2015 and 2020.KJ Alphons took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2006 and entered electoral politics in Kerala. He contested the Kanjirappally assembly seat in Kerala as an independent candidate supported by the Left Democratic Front and won.Alphons later founded the Jana Shakti platform before joining the BJP in 2011. His political journey subsequently took him to Parliament, when he became a Rajya Sabha member.In 2017, he was inducted into the Narendra Modi government as Union minister of state for tourism, with independent charge, and also handled electronics and information technology.His transition from a civil servant known for urban development initiatives to a state-level politician and Union minister is an example of an officer moving across political formations during his career.Satyapal Singh, a 1980-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, opted for voluntary retirement in January 2014 while serving as Mumbai police commissioner, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.He joined the BJP and contested the Baghpat Lok Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2014, defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Ajit Singh. He retained the constituency in the 2019 general election.Singh served as Union minister of state for human resource development and water resources during the Modi government's first term. Before entering politics, he had served in several police leadership roles and was known for his work in law enforcement.OP Choudhary, a 2005-batch IAS officer, resigned from the service in 2018 while serving as Raipur collector to enter politics. He joined the BJP and contested the Kharsia assembly constituency in Chhattisgarh in the same year.Choudhary lost that election but returned to the electoral contest in 2023, this time winning the Raipur City South seat. He was subsequently inducted into the Chhattisgarh government as a minister.His career highlights the uncertain transition from administration to politics. Unlike officers who win their first election, Choudhary's initial defeat did not end his political ambitions. He returned five years later and secured a place in the state Cabinet.Aparajita Sarangi, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, took voluntary retirement in 2018 while serving as joint secretary in the Union rural development ministry.She joined the BJP in November that year and contested the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Bhubaneswar. Sarangi won the seat, defeating Biju Janata Dal candidate Arup Patnaik.She retained the constituency in the 2024 general election, establishing herself as a BJP leader in Odisha.Sarangi's transition was particularly swift: she moved from a senior central government position to an electoral contest within months of leaving the service and subsequently secured two consecutive Lok Sabha victories.AK Sharma, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took voluntary retirement in January 2021, around 18 months before his scheduled superannuation.Sharma had spent a substantial part of his career working in the Prime Minister's Office and was associated with Narendra Modi's administration during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister and later as prime minister.After leaving the service, Sharma joined the BJP and was elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. He subsequently became a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, handling portfolios including urban development and energy.His move demonstrated how a senior bureaucrat with experience in the central administration could enter state politics and secure a position in the Cabinet without first contesting a direct assembly election.Asim Arun, a 1994-batch IPS officer, took voluntary retirement in January 2022 while serving as Kanpur police commissioner. He joined the BJP soon afterwards, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Arun contested the Kannauj assembly seat and won, entering a constituency associated with the Samajwadi Party. He was subsequently inducted into the Yogi Adityanath government.His political entry came within weeks of his voluntary retirement, making him one of the clearest recent examples of a serving police officer moving directly into electoral politics before the end of his career.K Annamalai, a 2011-batch IPS officer of the Karnataka cadre, resigned from the police service in September 2019, before completing his tenure. He had served as superintendent of police in Udupi and Chikkamagaluru districts before leaving the force.He joined the BJP in August 2020 and rose rapidly through the party's ranks. In July 2021, he was appointed the BJP's Tamil Nadu president, becoming one of the party's most prominent faces in the state.Annamalai contested the 2021 Tamil Nadu assembly election from Aravakurichi but lost to the DMK's R Elango. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, he contested from Coimbatore but lost to DMK candidate Ganapathi P Rajkumar.In June 2026, Annamalai quit the BJP following differences with the party leadership over its political strategy in Tamil Nadu and launched a new political movement, 'We The Leaders'. He said the movement would focus on "common man politics", challenge what he described as "cult and dynastic politics", and eventually evolve into a political party. He has outlined plans to contest the 2031 Tamil Nadu assembly elections.
Article Summary: Divya Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party, on Thursday. The party will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career.

Article Title: ‘Her misconceptions’: India rejects US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter rolls

NEW DELHI: India’s Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Thursday strongly pushed back against Indian-origin Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal 's social media post on the country's democratic framework and electoral procedures, calling it an "interference" in India's internal affairs."The remarks by @RepJayapal on India’s electoral and political processes are unacceptable interference in India’s internal affairs," he posted on X.Emphasising India’s longstanding record of conducting free and fair elections, Kwatra invited Jayapal for a “constructive conversation” to address her concerns."India is a vibrant democracy, with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections. Always open to constructive conversation with the Congresswoman to dispel her misconceptions," he added.Kwatra's response came after Jayapal alleged a sweeping removal of citizens from India's draft electoral list."I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls. This appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing here at home to undermine voting rights in a democracy," the Congresswoman said."Protecting democracies everywhere is essential work, and the Indian people — like the American people — deserve free and fair elections. Non-violent resistance movements are essential in these moments and I stand with the Indian people who are engaging in non-violent protests to counter anti-democratic efforts in India," she wrote in a follow-up post.Her remarks came amid the ongoing protests in India against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls exercise.According to data released by the Election Commission (EC), approximately 72 million entries were removed from draft electoral rolls across 13 states and Union territories during the initial two phases of the SIR.Furthermore, during the ongoing third phase, which encompasses the publication of draft lists across 18 states and UTs, the number of excluded electors totals 61.6 million.Addressing these omissions, the EC clarified that if a legitimate elector's name was accidentally omitted during the SIR process, the individual retains the right to apply for reinstatement through the claims and objections mechanism, followed by the submission of Form 6.
Article Summary: India’s Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Thursday strongly pushed back against Indian-origin Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's social media post on the country's democratic framework and electoral procedures. Kwatra's response came afterJayapal alleged a sweeping removal of citizens from India's draft electoral list.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Thursday questioned the Centre's “silence” on US secretary of state Marco Rubio's upcoming India visit, especially over US ambassador Sergio Gor's statement that US officials “expect” external affairs minister S Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai."It is not surprising that the US Ambassador to India has just given more details on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's forthcoming visit to Mumbai. It is also not wholly surprising to hear him say that Mr. Rubio will be meeting Govt of India officials in Mumbai," Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh posted on X.Ramesh described Gor's remark that US officials “expect” Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai as “extraordinary” and asked whether the Narendra Modi government had left it to someone other than the ministry of external affairs (MEA) to announce the external affairs minister's engagements within India.“Since when has the announcement of the external affairs minister’s meetings within India been left to someone other than the MEA spokesperson? India is learning about these developments from the US ambassador, just as it first learnt from Mr Rubio himself on the evening of May 10, 2025, that Operation Sindoor had been halted,” he said, referring to the India-Pakistan conflict in May 2025."Why is the MEA silent on the External Affairs Minister's tryst with Mr.Rubio in Mumbai?" the Congress MP added.Ramesh’s remarks came after Gor said during an interactive session that Rubio would meet Indian government officials in Mumbai. “We expect that minister Dr S Jaishankar will be there along with other individuals from Delhi, who will make a trip up there to see him in Mumbai,” Gor said.The US Department of State announced on Tesday that Rubio will visit India from October 17 to 22 to further strengthen energy cooperation. This will be his second visit to India, following his trip in May.He will first travel to Samarkand in Uzbekistan, followed by Mumbai and then Jamnagar in Gujarat.New Delhi has yet to formally announce the US secretary of state's visit to India.
Article Summary: Congress questions Centre's "silence" on US secretary of state Marco Rubio's upcoming India visit. US ambassador Sergio Gor said US officials “expect” external affairs minister S Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai. Rubio will visit India from October 17 to 22 to further strengthen energy cooperation.

Article Title: NHAI warning prompts IGI T3 parking operator to lift FASTag curbs
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The parking operator at Terminal 3 (T3) of Delhi airport has removed FASTag -based entry restrictions, bringing much-needed relief to passengers and visitors. The move came a day after Indian Highways Management Company Ltd (IHMCL), under NHAI, warned the acquiring bank associated with the parking facility of action after it emerged that the operator was using FASTag to regulate vehicle entry rather than solely for collecting parking fees.NHAI had also temporarily suspended FASTag-based parking payments, citing the violation.In a post on X, NHAI said, “NHAI would like to inform you that the matter was taken up with the relevant stakeholders to address the inconvenience faced by commuters. Following the intervention of the concerned authorities, restrictions on vehicles with FASTag at Terminal 3 (T3) of Delhi airport have been removed.”With this, the earlier system has been restored. The parking operator had recently started diverting vehicles without FASTag to the multi-level parking facility, causing inconvenience to users. Vehicles entering this facility often get stuck in queues, exceeding the free parking period and forcing motorists to pay parking fees.
Article Summary: The parking operator at Terminal 3 (T3) of Delhi airport has removed FASTag -based entry restrictions. The move came a day after Indian Highways Management Company Ltd (IHMCL), under NHAI, warned the acquiring bank associated with the parking facility of action.

Article Title: SC Bar Association files criminal contempt plea against Sanjay Raut, Nikhil Wagle
Article Text:
SCBA clarified that it did not seek to prevent fair and temperate criticism of the judiciary.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) on Thursday filed a criminal contempt petition against journalist Nikhil Wagle and Uddhav Sena leader Sanjay Raut over their disparaging remarks against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant.Attorney General R Venkataramani has since granted consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against the two under the Contempt of Courts Act.The statements came after Chief Justice of India (CJI) declined a request last week from a delegation of opposition parties to meet him in person. The CJI said the delegation could instead file a petition before the court.According to the petition, Wagle subsequently posted "**** you CJI!" on his X account in response to a report about the CJI's decision. However, Wagle later deleted his tweet and posted an apology.Raut's remarks to the media were carried by news agency IANS on X on October 12."We have also seen judges attending political programs of the BJP in states where it is in power, and chief ministers organizing dinners to welcome high court and Supreme Court judges," Raut was quoted as saying. The petition further states that he referred to photographs purportedly showing judges playing badminton with political figures in London."The aforementioned statement is false and contrary to records and is made to scandalise and diminish the authority of the Hon'ble Supreme Court," the petition states.The petition cites a June 19 order of the Delhi high court , which found that photographs circulated as being from a badminton event in London were actually from an event held at Thyagaraj Stadium in New Delhi in November 2025. The High Court had directed that the content be taken down.The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) clarified that it did not seek to prevent fair and temperate criticism of the judiciary, reported Bar and Bench.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) filed a criminal contempt petition against journalist Nikhil Wagle and Uddhav Sena leader Sanjay Raut. Wagle posted "**** you CJI!" on his X account in response to a report about the CJI's decision. Raut's remarks were carried by news agency IANS on X on October 12.

Article Title: EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
Article Text:
The EC's notice comes amid the SIR row.

Notice by EC

ECI's notice to states.

How's Special Revision different from SIR

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The El ec tion Commission (EC) has informed the states that it would be conducting a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states, including the poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa.In a letter to the chief electoral officers of the states and Union territories concerned, including Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa, the Election Commission said January 1, 2027, would be the qualifying date for the exercise.The Special Summary Revision (SSR) is intended to add eligible voters, especially young people and first-time electors, rectify errors in existing entries and ensure electoral rolls are accurate and up to date.The current term of the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly ends on May 22 next year. The tenures of the assemblies in Manipur, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand, which have 60, 40, 117 and 70 seats, respectively, are due to end on different dates in March 2027.Under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, the Election Commission is permitted to conduct elections "earlier than six months before the term expires".While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits.For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.The SIR of electoral rolls has triggered a political controversy, with opposition parties raising concerns over the deletion of voters' names and the possibility of eligible citizens being left out of electoral lists.The poll panel has maintained that the exercise is aimed at cleaning up electoral rolls by removing duplicate and ineligible entries, including those belonging to deceased voters, while ensuring that all eligible citizens are included.ALSO READ: ‘Anarchic, immature’: BJP targets Rahul over anti-CEC protests; claims misconduct with women cop However, opposition parties have questioned the process, alleging that the exercise could lead to genuine voters losing their right to vote. They have also raised concerns over documentation requirements, verification procedures and the possibility of disproportionate effects on vulnerable groups, including migrant workers, the elderly and economically disadvantaged people.One of the main concerns surrounding SIR is the potential deletion of eligible voters' names during the verification process.The dispute has also reached the Supreme Court , with petitions raising concerns about the manner in which the revision is being conducted. The legal debate centres on the Election Commission's authority to revise electoral rolls and the safeguards available to voters who challenge their exclusion.
Article Summary: The Election Commission (EC) has informed the states that it would be conducting a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states. The states are Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa. The current term of the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly ends on May 22 next year.

Article Title: India to Starlink: Comply with rules before entering market
Article Text:

Mittal: Ahead of Musk in queue for approval

NEW DELHI: Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch services in India as it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to set up domestic infrastructure, a senior govt official said Wednesday, sending a tough message to tech trillionaire Elon Musk that in order to do business in India he will have to abide by the law of the land.Govt has no objection to the satellite internet provider rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations before it can offer services in India, sources said. A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the "first hop", connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to set up "base stations" will help authorities to secure compliance with laws.Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio and Musk's Starlink are the three entities planning to start satellite communication services in India.Significantly, another message to Musk that he cannot expect to be an exception to the law came from Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal, who said Airtel's Eutelsat OneWeb satellite service might receive regulatory approvals ahead of Starlink, as it is "way ahead" in the approval queue, having applied nearly five years ago.He added that he will be "very happy" to get it at least a few days before Starlink.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal on Tuesday said his company deserved to get approval to start a satellite internet service before Elon Musk’s Starlink as Airtel’s Eutelsat OneWeb had submitted its application earlier.“I am significantly ahead in the queue from him. I applied five years back. I have my ground networks ready for three years. My satellites have been hovering over India for last five years... We will be happy to get it at least a few days before him,” said Mittal at Bloomberg New Economy Forum, in response to a query soliciting his views on Musk’s recent tirade, as he accused Indian telecom providers of preventing Starlink from entering the Indian market.Govt has denied Musk’s charge that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.
Article Summary: Starlink has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to set up domestic infrastructure, a senior govt official said. Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Mittal said Airtel's Eutelsat OneWeb might receive regulatory approvals ahead of Starlink, as it is "way ahead" in the approval queue.

Article Title: Stent safety concerns reach Centre after reports of complications with Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade has urged a review of coronary stent safety standards after reports of complications involving Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet Secretariat has taken up concerns over the safety and quality of coronary stents with the Union health ministry after a Rajya Sabha MP sought intervention following reports of complications involving Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka.In an October 5 letter, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan acknowledged a representation from Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade, a medical doctor, said it had been forwarded to the department of health and family welfare for appropriate action and a reply.Gopchade’s September 28 representation cited media reports that Sri Lanka’s regulator had directed the withdrawal of three models of Indian-manufactured drug-eluting stents over concerns including improper positioning, stent dislodgement, acute stent thrombosis and failure to expand properly. The reported issues were identified during an investigation by Sri Lanka’s Medical Device Evaluation Committee, according to the letter.The MP cautioned that the reported concerns might not all ultimately be substantiated, but said they warranted scrutiny of existing safeguards for device performance, clinical appropriateness and the detection of complications after implantation.The representation calls for more stringent pre-market testing of stents and delivery systems, including assessments of durability, deployment, expansion and dislodgement.It also seeks stronger clinical documentation to ensure stenting is performed only when medically indicated and alternatives are considered where appropriate.A key recommendation is end-to-end traceability through batch and serial numbers for every implanted stent, allowing affected devices and patients to be identified quickly if a safety alert emerges. The MP has also sought stronger adverse-event reporting, particularly for stent thrombosis, migration, incomplete expansion, deformation and delivery-system complications.The representation further calls for a mechanism to swiftly review safety alerts, recalls and withdrawals issued by foreign regulators when the same or similar devices are marketed in India. Better patient follow-up and long-term safety data collection have also been proposed to detect emerging risks early.Citing regulatory guidance from the US, the UK and Canada, Gopchade highlighted the importance of engineering and durability testing, clinical evidence, traceability and timely regulatory action when safety signals emerge. He urged the health ministry and the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to examine the issues with cardiology experts and other stakeholders.The Cabinet Secretariat’s communication does not establish that the government has accepted the allegations, ordered a formal investigation or approved new regulatory measures. The reported concerns also do not, by themselves, establish that similar complications have occurred in India.
Article Summary: Cabinet Secretariat has taken up concerns over the safety and quality of coronary stents with the Union health ministry. Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade has sought intervention following reports of complications involving Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka.

Article Title: Fees for professional courses can be hiked midstream only in exceptional cases: SC
Article Text:
SC quashed a 37% fee hike for BTech courses for the 2023- 27 cohort at Dr BC Roy Engineering College in West Bengal.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a relief to students pursuing professional courses like engineering and medicine in private colleges who have to face a fee hike midstream, Supreme Court has held that any change in fee structure after admission can be allowed only in exceptional circumstances.While appreciating the contribution of self-financing institutions to the education sector, a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said there should be certainty regarding fees, and students must not be forced to pay more than that prescribed at the time of admission."For the overwhelming majority of households, the fee payable for a professional course constitutes a substantial part of the family's income and savings; it is not a matter of incidental expenditure. The parents make provisions for the fees... with the aspiration that their children will acquire better qualifications, secure better opportunities and build a future that may be better than their own. Many students and families also depend on educational loans to finance professional higher education," SC said, noting fees charged in professional courses are reported to be 711% higher than in general courses.The court said it was a matter of good governance for the state and its regulatory bodies to create an ecosystem in which there was certainty about the financial obligation that students and their families need to undertake to acquire professional qualifications."Adverse variations in financial commitment, and the insecurities that it may create, will impact the student and the family, and, in the long run, have an adverse effect on the quality and character of the professionals in the making. We are of the opinion that it is not difficult to formulate a scheme through which such uncertainties can be avoided," it said.SC quashed a 37% fee hike for BTech courses for the 2023-27 cohort at Dr BC Roy Engineering College in West Bengal. The college had also imposed a new development fee.Passing an order in favour of students who had challenged the fee hike, the bench said, "The regulatory regime for fixation of fees, as contemplated in the decisions of this court, AICTE regulations, National Education Policy 2020 coupled with principles of certainty, necessitates the relevant authorities to notify fee payable for the entire course before a student takes admission... Variation is permissible only in exceptional instances such as unforeseen increase in the expenditure. "
Article Summary: SC quashed a 37% fee hike for BTech courses for the 2023-27 cohort at Dr BC Roy Engineering College in West Bengal. The college had also imposed a new development fee. Fees charged in professional courses are reported to be 711% higher than in general courses.

Article Title: Can't write off AT-1 bonds of Yes Bank worth Rs 8.4k crore: SC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Bombay high court order which quashed a decision of the Yes Bank administrator to write off additional tier 1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore in March 2020.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih said, "We see no reason to interfere with the impugned judgement. The appeals are dismissed.""Putting the investors to such uncalled-for risk could have well been avoided. The purpose of the AT-1 bonds is imperative: it acts as a safety barrier to the bank from collapsing altogether. That purpose could have been served had RBI and Yes Bank acted in accordance with the terms of the Master Circular," the court said.The bench said RBI was "a mere bystander", allowing the CET1 ratio of Yes Bank to drop to "an astonishing low of 0.6% while the business of Yes Bank was being carried out in a clandestine manner"."It can't be denied material irregularities in functioning of Yes Bank were noticed much prior... However, to have the investors at the receiving end of the administrative lapses would be highly unfair," SC said. pti
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Bombay high court order which quashed a decision of the Yes Bank administrator to write off additional tier 1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore in March 2020. Article Title: No reservation for OBC, Dalits who convert: Supreme Court
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled a Scheduled Castes/OBC person who converts from a Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order will not be entitled to the benefits of reservation. The court held that reservation is attached to a constitutionally identified class and not to an individual as a personal entitlement, which can be transferred if a person converts.SC said backwardness suffered by the person in Hindu religion cannot be carried forward to the new religion embraced by him or her.The order came on a petition filed by then DMK-led Tamil Nadu govt challenging a Madras HC order quashing state govt's order to allow reservations for Dalit and OBC converts to Islam.As reservation is provided to some communities of other religions, which are recognised as backward classes in different states, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar held that conversion of OBCs/Dalits to a non-Hindu social order does not, by itself, confer membership of any particular notified backward class community of the adopted religion.The apex court's verdict comes against the backdrop of growing demand for extending reservation to those OBCs/Dalits who converted to other religions."A person who converts from a Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim affirmative action under Article 16(4) of Constitution merely on the basis of the social backwardness associated with his pre-conversion status; the backwardness suffered in the antecedent social order cannot, by itself, be carried forward so as to confer upon him the status of a backward class in the religion to which he has converted," Supreme Courtsaid while quashing the Tamil Nadu order.
Article Summary: SC said backwardness suffered by the person in Hindu religion cannot be carried forward to the new religion embraced by him or her. Order came on a petition filed by then DMK-led Tamil Nadu govt challenging a Madras HC order quashing state govt's order to allow reservations for Dalit and OBC converts to Islam.

NEW DELHI: To prevent CNG vehicles without a valid cylinder hydrotest certificate from refuelling, Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) on Thursday launched an artificial intelligence-enabled vehicle recognition system at 10 CNG stations in the capital.The system uses station cameras to capture vehicle registration numbers, which are processed through an AI application linked to the online Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) portal to verify the hydrotest status of CNG cylinders. “If a cylinder’s certification has expired or is invalid, automated alerts are immediately sent to station staff via handheld devices, LED displays and public announcement systems, enabling quick action before refuelling,” IGL said.The AI system supplements the existing manual checks carried out by station staff. CNG cylinders must undergo hydrotesting once every three years at PESO-approved testing centres. Following a cylinder blast at a retail outlet in the capital in Aug, PESO had asked all city gas distribution companies to strictly enforce safety norms at CNG stations. The vehicle involved in the blast had additional cylinders illegally mounted on it.IGL said the system would soon be installed at all its CNG stations across Delhi-NCR and other cities under its jurisdiction. The company operates over 300 CNG stations across 12 geographical areas covering 32 districts in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan. CNG is also available at nearly 650 petrol pumps operated by oil marketing companies.The pilot project was launched by PESO joint chief controller of explosives (north circle) Sanjay Kumar Singh at the Shantipath CNG station.IGL's managing director Kumar Shanker said every vehicle entering an IGL station should undergo prescribed safety checks to protect customers, employees and the public.IGL said it had also strengthened its safety management plan for CNG station operations, with mechanisms to monitor compliance, identify violations, take corrective action and enforce penalties where necessary.
Article Summary: Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL) launches artificial intelligence-enabled vehicle recognition system at 10 CNG stations in the capital. System uses station cameras to capture vehicle registration numbers, which are processed through an AI application linked to the online Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) portal.

Article Title: Renewable energy expansion needs to be aligned with transmission readiness: Experts
Article Text:
According to govt, 8,133 gigawatt hour of solar power was curtailed or restricted during April-June 2026 due to transmission constraints and to maintain grid security. The mismatch highlights the need to synchronise the commissioning of generation projects with transmission lines and substations to ensure electricity reaches consumption centres.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: New Delhi: India needs to align power generation plans with the time required to build transmission infrastructure to meet future electricity demand reliably and affordably, energy sector experts said at RE: DIALOGUES 2026 in the capital.They flagged right-of-way constraints, the availability of transformers and the distance between renewable energy generation centres and consumption hubs as key challenges for power sector planning.The mismatch between renewable energy generation and transmission readiness has emerged as a major concern. According to ICRA data for May 2026, about 18.1 GW, or 33% of the 54.8 GW of recently commissioned renewable energy capacity, was relying on temporary grid access because permanent transmission infrastructure was incomplete. Delays in transmission lines and substations can leave completed solar and wind projects unable to evacuate their full generation capacity.The constraints are also leading to power curtailment. According to govt, 8,133 gigawatt hour of solar power was curtailed or restricted during April-June 2026 due to transmission constraints and to maintain grid security. The mismatch highlights the need to synchronise the commissioning of generation projects with transmission lines and substations to ensure electricity reaches consumption centres.The discussion, organised by Policy Perspectives Foundation and Orange Circle Energy, also highlighted the need to strengthen electricity distribution infrastructure, ensure regulatory stability and direct investments towards supporting infrastructure to meet rising demand.Bhupinder Bhalla, former secretary in the ministry of new and renewable energy, said India’s energy transition must be aligned with its wider development priorities, including domestic manufacturing, technology development, investment and job creation. He called for coordinated planning between the Centre and states to address infrastructure and regulatory challenges.Nikesh Sinha, founder of Orange Circle Energy, said India needs to look beyond its ability to generate electricity and assess how much power it will need, where demand will emerge and how reliably it can be delivered.“Transmission infrastructure takes time to build, and generation and consumption centres are not always in the same locations. Anticipating these requirements and aligning transmission planning with generation, while also considering decentralised solutions, will be critical to meeting India’s future electricity needs,” Sinha said.The experts also discussed the need to channel existing public resources towards priorities such as renewable energy and disaster resilience. Safi Ahsan Rizvi, former adviser to the National Disaster Management Authority and associated with the Policy Perspectives Foundation, said better allocation of existing resources could help unlock investment.
Article Summary: The mismatch between renewable energy generation and transmission readiness has emerged as a major concern. According to govt, 8,133 gigawatt hour of solar power was curtailed or restricted during April-June 2026 due to transmission constraints. The mismatch highlights the need to synchronise the commissioning of generation projects with transmission lines and substations.

Article Title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea to hold protest organisers liable for damage
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday sought responses from the Centre, Delhi Police and others on a plea seeking to hold organisers of protests personally or jointly liable for loss of life, injuries, damage to public or private property and the costs incurred by the authorities.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was hearing the petition, which also sought a direction that protests, dharnas, demonstrations, processions and public assemblies in the national capital should not be held without prior written permission from the competent authority.The plea sought to make organisers, callers, leaders or convenors of protests liable for losses arising from unlawful acts or omissions, including when an assembly is held without permission or violates the conditions imposed for its approval.The bench issued notices to the Centre, Delhi Police and other parties, seeking their responses to the petition, according to news agency PTI.The petition also sought directions to the authorities to identify and notify designated locations for protests, dharnas, demonstrations and public assemblies in Delhi. These sites, it said, should be situated away from densely populated, commercial and central areas.It further proposed that every application seeking permission for a protest, demonstration, procession or public assembly should be accompanied by an affidavit from the organiser disclosing the source of funding.The declaration should also specify whether any part of the funds had been received, or was expected to be received, from a foreign source or an unidentified source, the plea said.According to the petition, a false or incomplete declaration should provide grounds for revoking permission, recovering compensation and costs from the organiser and those found to have financed the assembly, and initiating prosecution in accordance with the law.The hearing came as the Supreme Court considered several petitions connected to protests in Delhi, including pleas concerning alleged assaults on journalists and lawyers, police action and restrictions on demonstrations.In a separate matter, the bench issued notices to the Centre and the Delhi government on a plea challenging the Delhi Police’s decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.The petitioner, advocate Swaty Malik, argued that removing the designation violated the fundamental right to protest. The plea maintained that demonstrations should be permitted at a location where protesters could make their grievances heard by the state administration.Justice Bagchi observed that the concept of being heard should also be considered in the context of technology.“The word ‘heard’ must be used in the perspective of technology also”, Justice Bagchi remarked.The court agreed to examine the petition and sought responses from the authorities.In other pleas linked to the protests, the Supreme Court sought responses from the authorities over allegations involving journalists and lawyers. It also directed law-enforcement agencies to preserve CCTV footage and other digital records relating to the demonstrations.The bench further directed that the order issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) be placed on record. The provision empowers authorised executive magistrates to issue urgent prohibitory orders to prevent public danger, disturbances or riots.The court indicated that the Union government would file a consolidated response to the batch of petitions while relevant material relating to individual cases was preserved.Separately, the Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission and chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on a petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 12 other opposition leaders over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The bench also took note of submissions concerning the October 12 march to the Supreme Court by Rahul and other opposition leaders.“Nobody can browbeat us (judiciary),” CJI Surya Kant said during the hearing, adding that the court was aware of statements made both inside and outside the courtroom.The court said it would ask one of the petitioners about his conduct at the next hearing, without naming the individual.The petition by Rahul and the other opposition leaders sought an independent audit of deletions and modifications made during the SIR, to be conducted by a committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge and assisted by technical experts and other prominent citizens.It also sought safeguards against deleting voters’ names without notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard, along with measures to allow eligible voters in Punjab and other poll-bound states to seek inclusion in electoral rolls within the time permitted by law.
Article Summary: Plea seeks to hold organisers of protests liable for loss of life, injuries, damage to public or private property and costs incurred by the authorities. Petition also seeks directions to the authorities to identify and notify designated locations for protests, dharnas, demonstrations and public assemblies in Delhi.

NEW DELHI: The southwest (summer) monsoon withdrew from the entire country on Thursday, exactly on the date of its normal withdrawal, while the northeast (winter) monsoon rainfall activity simultaneously commenced over part of south Peninsular India, IMD said.Summer monsoon normally starts withdrawing from west Rajasthan on Sept 17 and its withdrawal process ends on Oct 15. This year, the withdrawal started on Sept 19. Last year, the complete monsoon withdrawal happened by Oct 16.“With the onset of the northeast Monsoon, a wet spell with isolated heavy falls is likely over many parts of south Peninsular India till Oct 21,” said the Met department. The parts of south India that witnessed winter rainfall showers on Thursday include Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, south interior Karnataka and Kerala.IMD has already predicted a ‘normal’ winter monsoon in south Peninsular India during the Oct-Dec period. Overall, south Peninsular India receives about 30% of its annual rainfall during the northeast monsoon season (Oct to Dec). Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal receive approximately 48% of their annual rainfall during the season.Normal winter monsoon rainfall this year may bring some relief to the region, which received the fourth-lowest summer monsoon rainfall since 1901 and the second-lowest since 2001.Though the country as a whole recorded a deficit of nearly 13% during the June-Sept summer monsoon period — the fourth-lowest season since 2001 and 13th lowest since 1901 — the deficit in Karnataka was as high as 30% followed by 28% in Kerala, 25% in Andhra Pradesh and 20% in Tamil Nadu.

Article Title: Lula or Bolsonaro: Why Brazil's presidential election matters for Brics and India
Article Text:
Flávio Bolsonaro (right) leads the race into the runoff after securing 47& against Lula’s 45%.

(From left) Egyptian president Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Russian president Vladimir Putin, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chinese president Xi Jinping and South African president Cyril Ramaphosa during a joint tree plantation initiative during the 18th Brics Summit, at the Bharat Mandapam, in New Delhi.

Results after first round of voting in Brazil.

A bloc pulled in three directions

Brics continues to expand unlike the West-dominated G7.

Beyond one man’s fate

The Brics has outperformed G7 over the last two decades.

Brics constitutes 40% of the global GDP.

A state under strain

A woman at a voting centre in US to participate in Brazil's general election. (Reuters photo)

Where India stands

One in every four overseas Indians lives in Brics nation.

ALSO READ |

ALSO READ |

When Brics leaders met in New Delhi last month, Brazil’s President Lula da Silva was conspicuously absent from the Bharat Mandapam. He was campaigning for the crucial fourth term back home, so his foreign minister Mauro Vieira arrived in the capital for the "non-West" summit.That absence could now highlight the Brics' road ahead, at least for the time US President Donald Trump occupies the White House.Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. This is what Brics stood for when India hosted it on September 12. However, the real B of Brics, which is Brazil, has the world's attention.On 25 October, Brazilians will choose between Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of jailed ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, and the winner will decide how deeply one of the bloc’s founding members keeps investing in it.Flávio Bolsonaro leads the race into the runoff (second round of voting) after securing 47 per cent of the first-round vote, against Lula’s 45 per cent. Brazil mandates a second round of voting if no candidate secures a majority (more than 50 per cent) in the first round. Therefore, for a grouping already stretched by its own expansion, the result matters well beyond South America.Brics began with five members and grew to eleven after the 2024 expansion, with Indonesia the newest, joining in 2025.Brazil opposed the enlargement, particularly because of the one nation. Iran. It feared that adding the avowedly anti-West Islamic Republic would cost the group its cohesion. Like India, Brazil wants Brics to be reformist and not revolutionary, thereby limiting it to a body that argues for change inside the existing order rather than one that tries to replace it.Vieira, putting the Brazilian view plainly in the run-up to the 2026 summit, said that “a multipolar world that promises peace and prosperity must not be confused with a world of spheres of influence.” In other words, Brasília wants rules that bind the strong as well as the weak.Brazil had some success as the New Delhi declaration reaffirmed support for the United Nations system and the Paris climate agreement, going further than the G7, whose latest declarations did not mention the climate pact.However, these are words and not actions, and Russia, a Brics member, has ignored the UN Charter in recent years. Even so, agreeing to acknowledge the UN’s legitimacy was a better outcome than blocking any mention of it.Those gains on paper may not last, as Brazil’s place in the bloc will depend largely on its next president. The world’s two biggest powers have very different visions for what Brics should become. Both Washington and Beijing are seeking to tilt the balance in their favour.The United States, under Donald Trump, has made clear what it wants from Brazil. The Trump administration imposed heavy trade duties on Brazilian exports in July 2025, in retaliation for what it called a judicial “witch hunt” against former President Jair Bolsonaro, who Trump see as his "ally".It has sanctioned the Supreme Court justice who prosecuted him and revoked the visas of several justices. It also accepted Flávio Bolsonaro’s appeal in May to designate two Brazilian criminal groups as foreign terrorist organisations, while Lula’s alternative proposals went unanswered.A Bolsonaro win would help realign Latin America behind an America First agenda of militarised approaches to crime, crackdowns on migration and preferential access to critical minerals and energy. Brazil holds the world’s second-largest rare earth reserves, and Washington wants to reduce its dependence on China for them.On the trade and commerce front, Bolsonaro has criticised non-dollar initiatives, which is exactly the kind of de-dollarisation talk that makes some Brics ideas unwelcome in Washington. His platform does not mention Brics at all, and he has entertained the idea of leaving the group.Beijing sits on the other side of the ledger, and its leverage is economic. China has been Brazil’s largest trading partner since 2009. It buys nearly 30 per cent of Brazil’s total exports, including soybeans, crude oil and iron ore, and it has become a major investor in electricity, mining, cars and oil.A Brics that China hopes to make firmer and more assertive is difficult to build without Brazil, the largest economy in Latin America. That is why a Brazilian drift towards Washington would be felt in Beijing, even if it never became a formal exit.Nevertheless, the challenge with China is intricate, as even under Jair Bolsonaro, anti-Beijing rhetoric did not stop bilateral trade from reaching record levels, and Brazil resisted US pressure to exclude Huawei from its 5G rollout. Flávio Bolsonaro’s own programme envisages continued commercial engagement with China. A withdrawal from Brics, in short, is possible but far from inevitable.Therefore, a Bolsonaro government could stay inside the main multilateral bodies while withdrawing from the effort to give them energy, shifting from coalition-building among middle powers to a transactional, bilateral relationship with Washington.Lula, by contrast, has pursued what officials call “multi-alignment”, keeping a working relationship with the United States, expanding trade with China and using Brics, the G20 and UN climate talks to widen Brazil’s room for manoeuvre.The foreign policy debate is real, but it is not what most Brazilians say drives their vote. Crime is a central worry, and Bolsonaro’s “mano dura”, or iron fist, approach appeals to voters tired of violence in their neighbourhoods.Education is another concern, as a recent poll found that 71 per cent of Brazilians are weighing it in their vote, and 83 per cent believe it should be among the next government’s top three priorities.Only 66 per cent of Grade 2 children met basic literacy requirements in 2025, well short of the 80 per cent target for 2030.On the US relationship, voters appear to lean towards Lula. Polls show his popularity rose after his frequent disagreements with Trump over trade and security, and other surveys found Brazilians blamed Bolsonaro more for the tariffs imposed in July.The Brazilian Association of Institutional and Governmental Relations says the same pressure would follow Bolsonaro into office.Its president, Jean Castro, said: “He cannot adopt a stance that could be mistaken for subservience.”Behind these campaign themes lies a harder question. Can Brazil actually deliver on what it promises abroad? Brasilia's influence depends on partners believing that today’s deals will survive tomorrow’s politics, and that this belief is eroding.More than 90 per cent of the federal government’s non-interest spending is mandatory, leaving little room for infrastructure, which Brazil needs if it is to make use of its mineral reserves.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects that government debt will reach about 98 per cent of GDP by the end of 2026. Real interest rates sit near 10 per cent, so servicing that debt consumes funds that could strengthen security forces or support strategic goals.Adding to that, criminal networks operate across more than 1,500 clandestine airstrips in the Amazon basin and move drugs, gold and weapons across borders with Brazil’s ten neighbours.Responsibility for fighting them is split among federal police, highway police, an intelligence agency, police forces in 26 states and the federal district, the armed forces and prosecutors. Efforts to bring them under one authority have failed in Congress. The result is that decisions about gangs operating from Brazilian soil are increasingly taken elsewhere, as Washington’s terrorist designations show.The third problem is trust in the courts because since late 2025, the public has learned how far parts of the judiciary became entangled with the Banco Master affair.The bank’s owner is alleged to have made side payments and awarded lucrative contracts to families of Supreme Court justices, and to have lent his private jets to justices.Flavio Bolsonaro is himself under investigation over alleged links to the bank, and figures close to Lula’s government have also been drawn in.The winner will appoint at least three of the court’s 11 justices, reshaping the institution that is meant to hold the next government to account.The neighbourhood also offers little relief. Brazil once led the creation of regional institutions such as Mercosur, but it is now increasingly isolated in South America. Its relationship with Argentina, which helped underpin four decades of regional stability, has deteriorated to the point that neither country has an ambassador in the other’s capital.India could probably be the member with the most to lose from a Brics that becomes either a Chinese-led counterweight to the West or an empty shell.India has a significant interest in Brazil's political direction, given its economic ties with the Latin American nation. Bilateral trade exceeded $15 billion in 2025, making Brazil India's biggest trading partner in Latin America. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva have set a target of taking bilateral trade to $20 billion by 2030.Brazil's importance also extends to the steel sector, as the country is a major global supplier of iron ore and has substantial reserves of minerals used in steel production. Stronger cooperation could help India secure vital raw materials and access technologies needed to support the long-term expansion of its steel industry, according to a government statement.Flavio Bolsonaro, meanwhile, has indicated that he would not align himself exclusively with any side, naming India among the countries with which he would maintain engagement.India and Brazil have shared a strategic partnership since 2006, with collaboration covering areas such as defence, energy, agriculture, healthcare, critical minerals, technology and digital infrastructure.Beyond trade, the two countries coordinate on several international issues, including reform of the United Nations, climate change and counter-terrorism. Brazil is also India's largest trading partner across Latin America and the Caribbean.India hosted this year’s summit, where the Iranian and Emirati presidents both turned up, and it shares Brazil’s view that the bloc should push for reform rather than confrontation.The two countries also sit together in Partners for Multilateralism, launched on 21 September alongside Canada, Australia, Barbados, the European Union and Kenya.The framework is meant to support international law and institutional reform, and it links western and Global South middle powers without forcing any of them to pick a camp.That makes Lula a natural partner for New Delhi, and a Bolsonaro victory a quiet setback that could probably interrupt the bloc's ambitions.India would lose a like-minded voice for a measured, rules-based Brics, leaving it with partners who are either more radical or more distant. Its own position, balancing Washington and Beijing, depends on a bloc that can talk to both.However, whichever way Brazil votes, nobody expects an immediate revolution in its foreign policy.Rubens Ricupero, a former Brazilian diplomat, calls Bolsonaro’s approach a “blank slate”, while Lula’s is well established. The market for Brazil’s minerals, the weight of its trade with China and the limits on its finances will constrain either man. The pressure will come from outside.Rubens Barbosa, a former Brazilian ambassador to the US, warns that “the Americans may prove reluctant to yield anything to Lula, preferring to wait and negotiate with Bolsonaro.”Economist Monica de Bolle argues that a re-elected Lula facing a right-leaning Congress would feel “a lot of pressure” to give in “to some US demands regarding natural resources, as well as other issues.”That is the real stake for Brics on 25 October. The bloc’s future will turn on whether Brazil stays a champion of its reformist wing or becomes a member that merely turns up.
Article Summary: Brics has outperformed G7 over the last two decades. The world’s two biggest powers have very different visions for what Brics should become. Both Washington and Beijing are seeking to tilt the balance in their favour. Brazil opposed the enlargement, particularly because of one nation Iran.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecasted for isolated areas in the Northeast and South of India.

IMD alert for Tuesday

Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds

Northeast under heavy rain alert

South India forecast

Central and west India forecast

IMD's latest forecast for next few days
