Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: In 2011, Taylor Swift donated 6,000 books worth $68,000 to a Pennsylvania library that was struggling to stay open; 15 years later, it circulated 182,228 items and drew 27,452 program participants in
Article Text:
Rescuing branch services in Berks County

Expanding access and community engagement

Serving local patrons through targeted programs

When financial problems threatened to close public library branches across Berks County, Pennsylvania, a major donation from local native Taylor Swift helped keep them open for thousands of readers. In October 2011, the country music star donated 6,000 new books worth $68,000 (£52,000) to the Reading Public Library system. Fifteen years later, figures from the library network's official reports show that the system has grown into an important community resource. In 2025, it circulated 182,228 items and welcomed 27,452 people to its programs. Swift's donation came at a critical time, when cuts to local government budgets were putting heavy pressure on library services.Swift grew up nearby in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania. She learned about the Reading Public Library's money problems through local news reports and decided to help. According to reporting published by regional news outlet WHYY at the time, Swift bought thousands of popular books to refill empty shelves across all four city branches. Each donated book received a gold star on its spine and a special bookplate inside the front cover recognising the pop star's gift.The donation was shared equally among the main downtown library and three neighbourhood branches. This allowed readers across the wider Berks County library network to borrow the books. The arrival of many popular children's books, young adult novels, and general fiction helped library managers keep borrowing services running while local officials dealt with tight budgets.In the years after Swift's widely reported donation, the Reading Public Library expanded its services beyond lending books. It became an important place for residents to learn, find information, and connect with others. Figures published in the Reading Public Library's 2025 Annual Appeal report show the scale of its work today across four branches. In addition to lending more than 182,000 physical and digital items in 2025, the system recorded 77,812 public computer sessions lasting 30 minutes each. These sessions gave job seekers, students, and local families important access to the internet. The library also expanded its learning programs for people of all ages. In 2025, a total of 27,452 people attended its general programs. Another 3,207 young children took part in early childhood reading programs. Activities include storytimes for young children, after-school sessions for teenagers, and digital skills classes. These classes help older adults and people looking for work learn how to use modern technology.The library system depends on a mix of local government funding and private donations to keep its services running. According to information in the library's official 2025 Annual Appeal documents, staff members provide personal help to people in need every day. Examples highlighted by the library include one-on-one digital skills lessons for adults changing careers, help with mobile phone enrolment for older people on low incomes, and home book delivery for residents living in assisted care facilities. The library's official mission statement describes it as a welcoming place that supports the community through free access to information, help finding reliable resources, and opportunities to keep learning throughout life. The main downtown branch at 100 South Fifth Street continues to serve local residents. It is also the main centre for public library services across Berks County. Fifteen years after thousands of donated books arrived with gold stars on their spines, the library system continues to build on that support. It remains an important centre for reading, learning, and public education across central Pennsylvania.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.
Article Summary: Taylor Swift donated 6,000 books worth $68,000 (£52,000) to the Reading Public Library system in October 2011. The donation came at a critical time, when cuts to local government budgets were putting heavy pressure on library services. Fifteen years later, figures from the library network's official reports show that the system has grown into an important community resource. In 2025, it circulated 182,228 items and welcomed 27,452 people to its programs.

Article Title: Sara Blakely was selling fax machines door to door when she put $5,000 of her savings into Spanx; 21 years later, Blackstone bought a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation
Article Text:
Despite having no formal business education, Blakely developed her first product from her apartment (Picture: Spanx)

How Sara Blakely started with $5,000

Blackstone's major investment

Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon join

What changed for Spanx after investment?

In 2000, Sara Blakely was working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson when she decided to start her own business with $5,000 from her savings. Her idea was to develop a new type of women's undergarment that would offer greater comfort and support. However, she had no formal business training, had never attended a business class and had no outside investors. Nonetheless, she went on to establish Spanx, a company that would eventually become a major name in women's clothing.Twenty-one years later, in October 2021, global investment firm Blackstone announced an agreement to acquire a majority stake in the company at a valuation of $1.2 billion. The deal marked a major change for a business that Blakely had built without raising outside investment.According to Blackstone, Blakely would retain a significant ownership stake and continue working with the company's existing management team. She would also become Executive Chairwoman of Spanx.Alongside Blackstone, several prominent women, including Oprah Winfrey, Reese Witherspoon and Whitney Wolfe Herd, joined as investors. Their involvement brought together businesswomen who had previously supported the company or established successful companies of their own.Blakely's journey began while she was still selling fax machines door to door. She wanted to enter the women's shapewear and undergarment market, an industry that was male-dominated at the time.Despite having no formal business education, she worked on developing her first product from her apartment. She also wrote her own patent application for the undergarment she had invented.The company initially focused on shapewear, a category of clothing designed to provide support and create a smoother appearance under other garments. Over time, it expanded beyond original undergarments into several other clothing categories.Its product range eventually included leggings, denim, trousers, activewear, swimwear and intimate apparel. The company also introduced collections such as Perfect Pants, extending its business into everyday clothing.Blakely was also included in TIME magazine's list of the world's 100 most influential people and appeared on the cover of Forbes as the youngest self-made female billionaire.On October 20, 2021, Blackstone announced that funds managed by the investment firm had agreed to acquire a majority stake in Spanx. The agreement valued the entire company at $1.2 billion, although the exact amount Blackstone paid for its stake was not disclosed.Blakely welcomed the agreement while reflecting on how the company had started. “This is a really important moment in time for female entrepreneurs,” she had said.“I started this company with no business experience and very little money, but I cared the most about the customer, and that gave me the courage to launch the company,” she added,The transaction was formally completed on November 18, 2021, when Spanx and Blackstone announced the participation of several additional investors.Among them were television personality and entrepreneur Oprah Winfrey, actress and Hello Sunshine founder Reese Witherspoon, and Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd. Two female-founded investment firms, G9 Ventures and Able Partners, also participated.Winfrey had played a role in bringing the company to public attention during its early years. In 2000, she included the product in her well-known Favorite Thingsselection.Recalling her first experience with the product, Winfrey said, “When Sara first came on The Oprah Show to tell us about her idea for Spanx, I knew it was brilliant.”She added that the company had become a regular part of her wardrobe and expressed support for the company's continued development.Blakely also described the participation of Winfrey and Witherspoon as particularly meaningful because both had supported the brand for years.Under the agreement, Blakely retained a significant equity stake in Spanx and became its Executive Chairwoman. The existing senior management team also remained involved in overseeing daily operations.Blackstone and Spanx announced plans to establish an all-female board of directors. The Blackstone investment team responsible for the transaction was also made up entirely of women. The transaction also formed part of Blackstone's investments in female-founded businesses.Beyond her business career, Blakely is also committed to philanthropy. In 2013, she signed the Giving Pledge, promising to donate half her wealth to charitable causes. Through her personal foundation, she has already contributed millions of dollars towards supporting women.
Article Summary: Sara Blakely was working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson when she decided to start her own business with $5,000 from her savings. Her idea was to develop a new type of women's undergarment that would offer greater comfort and support. In October 2021, global investment firm Blackstone announced an agreement to acquire a majority stake in the company at a valuation of $1.2 billion. Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joined as investors.

Article Title: Microsoft president Brad Smith says it's ironic that White House targeted his company the same day it gave a medal to former H-1B Satya Nadella
Article Text:
Microsoft president Brad Smith reacts to the Trump administration's suspension of his company's Green Card applications.

What Microsoft said in its statement

No salary discrepancy

Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith reacted to the Donald Trump administration suspending the Green Card filings from his company along with seven other tech majors in an exclusive interview with Politico in Dublin and warned that this could cripple the US tech sector for over a generation. He said it was ironic that the White House chose to target his company’s foreign workers on the same day it gave a medal to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella , who was once an H-1B visa holder from India.“We should consider the fact that when the president honored six Americans with these technology and science medals, five of the six had come to the United States as immigrants,” Smith said. “And those five individuals, if you put them and their companies together, have companies that have a market value equal to more than 25% of the market value of the total S&P 500.”“Think about what those five individuals have done for the well-being, even the wealth and standard of living, of Americans across the country. Let’s not put that at risk.”Smith said JD Vance 's allegations of visa fraud are completely off base and that someone must have failed to inform the vice president of Microsoft's number accurately, because a majority of Microsoft's Green Card applicants are long-time employees and not new hires.The company had issued a statement immediately after JD Vance announced the PERM ban on eight tech companies."We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country," Microsoft said."Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category. We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," the statement added.Brad Smith said the company hired 9,000 US-born workers last year which the narrative set by the White House missed. “We will stand by our record,” said Smith. “And I hope that folks at the White House might look again and look at what we think is a more accurate picture.”Smith said the crackdown should worry US that they would not be able to attract top tech talent anymore. “I think we should all be worried about sending — intentionally or inadvertently or otherwise — signals that send the most talented next wave of AI [or] SI software engineers to other countries, rather than the United States,” he said.
Article Summary: Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith reacted to the Donald Trump administration suspending the Green Card filings from his company along with seven other tech majors. Smith warned that this could cripple the US tech sector for over a generation. He said it was ironic that the White House chose to target his company’s foreign workers on the same day it gave a medal to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.

Article Title: After Jio's listing, Reliance Industries could topple Tata as India's most valuable group
Article Text:
Reliance Jio Infocomm chairman Akash Ambani and non-executive director Isha Ambani at the IPO announcement in Mumbai Thursday

Jio carries more than 60% of India's data traffic: Akash

MUMBAI: In the biggest reshuffle in the country's corporate rankings in decades, Reliance Industries (RIL) Group is all set to overtake Tata Group as India's most valuable conglomerate, once Jio Platforms lists.The proposed listing, at an estimated valuation of Rs 10.3 lakh crore at the upper end of the Rs 1,065-1,119 per share price band, would lift RIL Group's market capitalisation to about Rs 28.5 lakh crore, ahead of Tata Group's Rs 25.5 lakh crore as of Oct 15, according to ET Intelligence data.RIL Group stood at Rs 18.2 lakh crore before the listing. The Jio Platforms IPO is expected to raise Rs 30,188 crore, making it India's largest primary offering. It is RIL Group's first IPO in nearly two decades."RIL Group, after Jio's listing, will be India's largest conglomerate by market cap under the leadership of Mukesh Ambani ," Uday Kotak said at the Jio Platforms media briefing.Banker Uday Kotak hailed the Jio Platfoms IPO as "a testament to the development of the next generation of leadership", naming Akash and Isha Ambani.The Adani Group currently ranks third with a market cap of Rs 17.48 lakh crore, followed by HDFC Group at Rs 13.91 lakh crore and Bajaj Group at Rs 13.88 lakh crore, according to ET Intelligence.An analyst said the listing would do more than raise capital. "Currently, Jio's value is embedded within Reliance Industries. A separate listing will unlock that holding company discount," he said. The combined market capitalisation of Reliance Industries and Jio Platforms would put clear daylight between the RIL and Tata groups, the analyst added. Isha Ambani said the idea for Jio emerged around 2009-10, when she and her twin brother, Akash, returned to Mumbai from college in the US. "I had an assignment to submit online. I tried to submit the assignment, but unfortunately the internet did not work, and I couldn't submit it," she said. The episode convinced Akash that India needed a digital technology platform company. Jio launched in 2016.Akash Ambani said Jio went from "the 14th operator to enter the market in 2016" to become India's largest telecom operator, carrying more than 60% of India's data traffic.
Article Summary: Reliance Industries (RIL) Group is all set to overtake Tata Group as India's most valuable conglomerate, once Jio Platforms lists. The proposed listing, at an estimated valuation of Rs 10.3 lakh crore at the upper end of the Rs 1,065-1,119 per share price band, would lift RIL Group's market cap to about Rs 28.5 lakh crore.

Article Title: Is there govt scheme to help pregnant minor rape survivors become self-reliant?: Bombay HC to Maharashtra govt
Article Text:
Bombay HC





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has asked state govt whether it has a scheme to assist girls who are survivors of sexual assault and are required to undergo medical termination of pregnancy to become self-reliant.“In our view, financial assistance alone may not provide a sustainable solution in the long run. However, if such a girl is imparted appropriate skills or is enabled to pursue her education, she may become self-reliant and would not have to depend upon financial assistance granted by this court,” said Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish Chavan on Monday.On Oct 9, they allowed MTP of the 28-week pregnancy of a 15-year-old sexual assault survivor and directed the petition to be tagged with two other petitions where two teenaged survivors were allowed to terminate their 25-week pregnancies. In a few matters, HC had indicated to the state to suggest some “methodology” by which such survivors “are assisted in any manner”.State’s advocate M P Thakur submitted a Govt Resolution (GR) issued by the women and child development department that set out a scheme under the Juvenile Justice Act and its rules.The judges noted the GR covers “various categories of children who are victims of offences” under the POCSO Act but “does not specifically identify this category…”“A girl who is a victim of an offence under the POCSO Act falls in a completely different category,” the bench said.“It is not necessary that, in every such case, she must be admitted to an institution or an observation home. Rather, the focus should be on enabling her to overcome the trauma with the assistance of her family members, while simultaneously making arrangements for her future so that she can become self-reliant and secure a means of livelihood. ”The judges said they “expect” Thakur to obtain instructions whether women and child development or social welfare departments have formulated any scheme “for the benefit of girls falling in this category”.The judges also asked to check with the women and child development commissioner whether there exists any scheme “specifically” for survivors of offences under POCSO Act, “apart from Manodhairya scheme, or whether any other scheme which provides financial assistance to such victims”.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court asked state govt whether it has a scheme to assist girls who are survivors of sexual assault. Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish Chavan said financial assistance alone may not provide a sustainable solution in the long run. They allowed MTP of the 28-week pregnancy of a 15-year-old sexual assault survivor.

Article Title: India-US trade deal: First phase finalised, legal drafting under way, says Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
India-US trade deal

The much-awaited India-US trade deal has cleared its first phase and moved to the legal drafting stage, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday.He said that the pact would be operationalised once India gains a competitive advantage over its peer countries. The minister further expressed hope that the process would be completed soon."US bilateral trade agreement's first tranche has been finalised and it is going through final contours, the legal drafting and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we get the competitive advantage over our peer countries," Goyal said.The minister also provided an update on India's trade negotiations with the European Union, saying that the free trade agreement would be signed in December and is expected to take effect in February or March next year.Earlier in the day, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor also said that the two nations have cleared the major items on their trade deal checklist. Gor described the pace of negotiations as “incredible.”Gor also spoke about the US legislation that could pave the way for sanctions on countries purchasing Russian oil and gas or helping others evade sanctions. He said US President Donald Trump was expected to decide on the matter within the next 10 days.The legislation received 86 votes in the 100-member US Senate and gives the President the authority to impose sanctions on countries involved in buying Russian oil and gas or facilitating sanctions evasion. Gor said the provisions were not aimed at any particular country, including India.“...We have ongoing discussions on that as it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. That law got 86 votes out of 100 in our Senate... These sanctions options that Congress passed, they are not targeted at any individual country. It is three different buckets; one is oil, the second is gas, the third is sanctions evasion.”Explaining how countries could fall within the scope of the measures, Gor said their inclusion was based on numbers. He added that India was among several countries that fell into one of the categories, but said the intention was to end the war rather than punish any country.“It just happens that India does fall in one of those buckets, along with a lot of other countries. The goal is not to punish anyone. The goal is to try to bring an end to this war. I do think the president will make a determination on that over the next few days.”Gor said India offered significant opportunities for American businesses, citing the size of its market and the government's approach to foreign investment.India and the US have been negotiating a proposed bilateral trade agreement since early 2025, seeking to address tariff-related tensions, remove non-tariff barriers and improve market access. India is also pushing for more favourable tariff terms for its exports to the US than those available to competing economies.
Article Summary: The much-awaited India-US trade deal has cleared its first phase and moved to the legal drafting stage, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said. He said that the pact would be operationalised once India gains a competitive advantage over its peer countries. Goyal also provided an update on India's trade negotiations with the European Union, saying that the free trade agreement would be signed in December and is expected to take effect in February or March next year.

Article Title: Direct tax mop-up rises 13.21% to Rs 13.38 lakh crore till October 14
Article Text:
Net direct tax collections rise 13.21% to Rs 13.38 lakh crore

NEW DELHI: India's net direct tax mop-up reached Rs 13,37,866.98 crore in FY2026-27 as of October 14, marking a 13.21 per cent increase from Rs 11,81,786.98 crore collected during the same period last year, data released by the income tax department showed.The increase came alongside a rise in gross collections, which climbed to Rs 16,03,066.12 crore from Rs 13,95,278.39 crore in the year-ago period. However, the amount returned to taxpayers also increased, with refunds rising 24.22 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,65,199.14 crore from Rs 2,13,491.41 crore.Net corporate tax receipts stood at Rs 5,99,062.48 crore as of October 14, compared with Rs 4,96,798.62 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.Gross corporate tax collections rose to Rs 7,52,961.56 crore from Rs 6,43,721.45 crore. Refunds issued against corporate tax increased to Rs 1,53,899.08 crore, up from Rs 1,46,922.83 crore in the same period last year.Net non-corporate tax collections increased to Rs 6,91,965.71 crore from Rs 6,53,804.16 crore a year earlier. This category includes taxes paid by individuals, Hindu Undivided Families, firms and other entities.Gross collections under the non-corporate tax category rose to Rs 8,03,245.26 crore, compared with Rs 7,20,353.91 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.Refunds in this category registered a more pronounced increase, reaching Rs 1,11,279.55 crore against Rs 66,549.75 crore a year earlier.Collections from the Securities Transaction Tax (STT) rose to Rs 46,840.43 crore as of October 14, compared with Rs 30,901.81 crore in the corresponding period last year. The increase reflected higher collections from transactions in securities.The overall figures show that the rise in gross direct tax receipts was accompanied by a faster increase in refunds. While gross collections grew 14.89 per cent year-on-year, refunds increased 24.22 per cent, bringing the growth in net direct tax collections to 13.21 per cent.The data covers collections up to October 14 and provides a snapshot of direct tax receipts during the first half of the current financial year.
Article Summary: India's net direct tax mop-up reached Rs 13,37,866.98 crore in FY2026-27 as of October 14. This is a 13.21 per cent increase from Rs 11,81,786.98 collected during the same period last year. Refunds issued against corporate tax increased to Rs 1,53,899.08 crore.

Article Title: Kospi hits the brakes: South Korean benchmark plunges 7.5%, triggers 'sidecar' stop for investors
Article Text:
Kospi tumbles over 7% as tech stocks lose steam

Samsung, SK Hynix lead South Korean market rout

‘Sidecar’ triggered

South Korea’s stock market hit a rough patch on Thursday, with the benchmark Kospi plunging 7.49% as technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The rout spread across Asian markets, prompting the country’s exchange operator to trigger a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures.The KOSPI dropped 450.02 points to 5,558.79, putting it on course for a seventh consecutive session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024. The index has fallen nearly 35% from its record high in June.The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated more than expected in September. The data fuelled concerns that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this year, putting technology companies and AI-related stocks under further pressure.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 3.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 4.8%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.5%.Major technology companies accounted for some of the steepest losses on the South Korean exchange. Samsung Electronics shares fell 9.05%, while SK Hynix dropped 11.06%, reflecting the broader weakness across Asia’s semiconductor supply chain.Battery maker LG Energy Solution lost 3.44%. Hyundai Motor declined 3.99%, while sister automaker Kia Corp fell 2.03%.The selling extended to other Asian technology companies. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell 2%, while Japan’s memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plunged more than 11%. SoftBank Group, an investor in AI, declined 9.4%.Market breadth in South Korea remained heavily negative. Of the 889 stocks traded, 768 declined and 90 advanced. Foreign investors sold shares worth a net 355.6 billion won.The won, meanwhile, strengthened 0.21% to 1,339.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, compared with its previous close of 1,342.3.The sharp decline prompted the South Korean exchange operator to activate a sell-side “sidecar”, an automatic mechanism designed to temporarily cool trading during periods of heavy selling. The measure suspends program sell orders for five minutes after steep losses in index futures.The trigger came as the KOSPI extended its decline to seven consecutive sessions. The benchmark has now shed nearly 35% since its June record, with retail investors among those hit hardest during a sell-off in July, when the index fell around 20%. Losses in highly leveraged single-stock exchange-traded funds (ETFs) contributed to the damage during that period.The sell-off in Asia followed Wall Street’s third consecutive session of losses. The S&P 500 declined 1.1% overnight, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%. A gauge of semiconductor stocks recorded its sixth straight day of losses as investors reassessed the outlook for companies sensitive to borrowing costs.Meanwhile, in South Korea’s bond market, December futures on three-year treasury bonds rose 0.12 point to 103.00. The yield on the most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond fell 3 basis points to 3.855%, while the benchmark 10-year yield declined 2.1 basis points to 4.224%.Oil prices also moved lower, with Brent crude falling 1.7% to $104.20 a barrel. Traders weighed the potential impact of US sanctions relief on oil supply against attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Kospi plunges 7.49% as technology stocks come under heavy selling pressure. The country’s exchange operator triggered a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures. The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Delhi-NCR, IMD issues orange alert
Article Text:
Heavy rain and thunderstorms impacted multiple areas of Delhi-NCR on Thursday

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi-NCR on Thursday, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds sweeping across the region.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital.The weather department forecast rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds blowing at 40-60 kmph.The alert remained in force until 2 pm, with intermittent spells of rain expected in several parts of Delhi, the IMD said.The minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal. The maximum temperature is expected to hover around 29 degrees Celsius, bringing down daytime temperatures, it said.Experts attributed the sudden spell of rain to a western disturbance and a cyclonic circulation over adjoining areas.They said the conditions were part of a normal post-monsoon weather pattern, with Delhi and other parts of the region likely to receive intermittent showers.
Article Summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital. Rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. Minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Elon Musk's 'China prediction' may add to the pain of 20 of the most valuable global technology companies across US and Europe that have lost over $1 trillion dollars in less than 5 days
Article Text:
Elon Musk's 'China prediction' may add to the pain of 20 of the most valuable global technology companies across US and Europe that have lost over $1 trillion dollars in less than 5 days

Here's how much Nvidia , AMD, Micron and other companies lost

Why AI and semiconductor stocks are selling off

A sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor shares has wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value from 20 of the world’s most valuable technology companies in less than five days, a report has said. It attributes this to a combination of interest rate hikes, increasing AI infrastructure costs and intensifying competition. Adding to the anxiety, Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced plans to accelerate its memory chip manufacturing capabilities, putting fresh pressure on an already rattled global market. Elon Musk reacted to the news saying that China will be making “a LOT of RAM in 2028”, a view that could add to that pressure.The billionaire’s commentary arrives as investors grapple with growing anxiety over an impending global memory chip oversupply as early as 2029, spurred by chipmakers worldwide aggressively building out production capacity to meet AI workloads. CXMT recently said that it achieved a major architectural breakthrough to boost memory density by packing more data into tighter spaces.US semiconductor giants and specialised cloud infrastructure providers continued to slide in premarket trading on Thursday (October 15) following a punishing Wednesday session on Wall Street.Nvidia fell 1.8%; Micron Technology dropped 4.4%; AMD slipped 3.5%; Oracle traded down 2%; Neocloud providers took sharp hits, with CoreWeave falling 5.3% and Nebius retreating 4%.Notably, the rout was not confined to US exchanges, deepening across major trading hubs in Asia and Europe. South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix plummeted more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics dropped 8.73%. Related tech and component suppliers saw steep declines as well, with LG Innotek sinking 8.95%, Seoul Semiconductor sliding 9.28%, and Samsung SDI down 6.26%.In Japan, technology investment firm SoftBank Group tumbled 7.9%. Testing equipment supplier Advantest plunged nearly 14%, Tokyo Electron lost 6.45%, and Renesas Electronics fell 8%. Similarly, in Taiwan, leading contract foundry TSMC slipped 1.81%. When it comes to Europe, advanced lithography supplier ASML traded down 6.6%, ASM International sank 9.6%, Germany’s Infineon Technologies lost 9.4%, and Nokia dropped 5%.Market analysts and investors point to a convergence of macroeconomic headwinds, financing bottlenecks, and long-term supply threats that are eroding sentiment across the sector. Inflation has raised concerns that elevated interest rates will increase the cost of capital needed to finance massive data center and AI infrastructure deployments.Top industry leaders have voiced caution regarding capital access. On Monday, the chief executives of Broadcom and Intel warned that financing could soon become the primary headwind facing the AI boom.
Article Summary: 20 of the world's most valuable technology companies have lost over $1 trillion dollars in less than 5 days. The rout was not confined to US exchanges, deepening across major trading hubs in Asia and Europe. South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix plummeted more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics dropped 8.73%.

Article Title: 56 year old Chestnut trees, said to be one of America’s last remaining Chestnut Groves, at risk of being wiped out by datacenter labelled as: 'One of the largest single AI infrastructure investments i
Article Text:
Why the West Virginia chestnut grove matters

What is the Monarch Compute Campus

A conflict between AI infrastructure and conservation

In 1904, a necrotrophic fungus called chestnut blight began devastating North America's native chestnut trees. This fungus, brought across the Pacific on chestnut trees from Japan and China, attacks tree bark and kills the above-ground portions of susceptible trees. The disease eventually wiped out billions of chestnut trees across the US. More than a century later, a grove of approximately 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees in West Virginia is facing the threat of being cleared to make way for a large-scale artificial intelligence data center.Planted in the 1970s, the 56-year-old trees are a valuable source of genetic material that could help restore the species. However, the proposed Monarch Compute Campus, developed by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar, could put the grove at risk. The project is planned to span more than 2,250 acres and provide 8 gigawatts of computing capacity, with its developer calling it “one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history. ”The chestnut blight outbreak destroyed an estimated 4 billion American chestnut trees across the US.Although surviving stumps can produce new shoots, these often succumb to the disease before reaching maturity.Researchers and horticulturists have since worked to preserve the species through breeding programmes and blight-resistant hybrids. However, mature chestnut groves remain uncommon. According to the supplied report, fewer than 4,300 acres of fruit-producing chestnut trees existed across the continental US in 2023.The grove contains about 200 blight-resistant chestnut trees planted in the 1970s from surviving wild American chestnuts. Their age and genetic material make them a potentially important resource for future restoration efforts.A report published in From the Front Lines: Struggles for Justice by the New York-based Global Justice Ecology Project has raised concerns about the grove's future.“Planted in the 1970s from wild surviving American chestnuts, this orchard is a vital ‘genetics library,'” the publication explains, describing it as “the primary seed source to restore the species across West Virginia.”The trees could provide seeds and genetic material for efforts to establish new chestnut populations. Losing the grove could therefore affect more than the existing trees, potentially reducing the resources available to future restoration projects.The proposed data center development is being built by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar. Under the current plans, the completed campus will cover more than 2,250 acres and provide 8 gigawatts of computing capacity for AI companies, including Anthropic.The development represents a substantial investment in computing infrastructure as technology companies expand their capacity to train and run artificial intelligence models.Nscale has described the project as “one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history, anchoring America’s compute foundation.”The scale of the planned facility could make protecting the grove difficult, especially if the trees fall within areas designated for construction.The potential loss of the chestnut grove highlights a conflict between expanding AI infrastructure and preserving biological resources. Data centers require large sites, electricity and supporting infrastructure, while conservation projects depend on protecting habitats and maintaining genetic diversity.According to From the Front Lines, the surviving chestnut trees are “irreplaceable” because they could support future restoration work.The grove's future will depend on the development plans and whether its preservation can be reconciled with construction. For conservationists, protecting these trees could help retain an important source of genetic material for restoring American chestnuts to their former range.
Article Summary: A grove of 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees in West Virginia is facing the threat of being cleared to make way for a large-scale artificial intelligence data center. The 56-year-old trees are a valuable source of genetic material that could help restore the species. The proposed Monarch Compute Campus, developed by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar, could put the grove at risk.

Article Title: Microsoft president Brad Smith breaks silence on the US government suspending Microsoft from Green Card sponsorship programme; says: We should all be worried about ...
Article Text:
In pic: Microsoft president Brad Smith

What Microsoft president Brad Smith said

Microsoft president Brad Smith rejects visa fraud accusations against the company

Microsoft president Brad Smith has warned that the US government’s move suspending Microsoft and other tech giants from the Green Card sponsorship programme could hurt the country’s ‌technological competitiveness and drive talent overseas. In an exclusive interview with Decoded by Politico, Brad Smith pushed back against Vice President JD Vance's accusations that Microsoft had abused the H-1B visa ⁠program, calling them "completely off base". He also pointed at the irony that the White House put restrictions on Microsoft on the same day it gave a medal to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, a former H-1B skilled visa holder from India.Expressing concerns about the impact the crackdown on the ability of the U.S. to attract top tech talent, Smith said: “I think we should all be worried about sending — intentionally or inadvertently or otherwise — signals that send the most talented next wave of AI [or] SI software engineers to other countries, rather than the United States”. Notably, Brad Smith’s comments come almost a week after the US government announced that it will bar Microsoft, TCS, Infosys and other companies from seeking green cards for skilled foreign ​workers.During the interview, Microsoft president Brad Smith said: “We should consider the fact that when the president honored six Americans with these technology and science medals, five of the six had come to the United States as immigrants,” adding “And those five individuals, if you put them and their companies together, have companies that have a market value equal to more than 25% of the market value of the total S&P 500. ”“Think about what those five individuals have done for the well-being, even the wealth and standard of living, of Americans across the country. Let’s not put that at risk,” he continued.Brad Smith also rejected JD Vance’s visa fraud accusations and called the vice president’s claims “completely off base.” He said someone “had failed to inform the vice president accurately about our numbers,” noting that the “vast majority” of Microsoft’s green card applications were for long-time employees, not new hires.“Unfortunately, it’s just because the green card backlog is so long,” said Smith.Denying that the company pays foreign-born workers less, the Microsoft executive said “it doesn’t matter whether you came on a visa or you’re an American worker, everybody has the same compensation system.” And he complained that the more than 9,000 U.S.-born workers that Microsoft hired last year were “left out of the narrative” propagated by the White House.“We will stand by our record,” said Smith. “And I hope that folks at the White House might look again and look at what we think is a more accurate picture.”
Article Summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith has warned that the US government’s move suspending Microsoft and other tech giants from the Green Card sponsorship programme could hurt the country's technological competitiveness. Brad Smith pushed back against Vice President JD Vance's accusations that Microsoft had abused the H-1B visa program.
